subject: GPU tuning and burst heuristics for Dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Kai Watanabe <kai@lumosai.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: sandeep@lumosai.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity feasibility — Peak bursts & tail latency

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this. Quick summary of what we're seeing on Lumos Chat (customer-facing assistant):
- Steady-state: ~1,200 requests/minute (RPS ~20) across multiple regions.
- Burst behavior: intermittent marketing prompts drive short spikes up to ~6,000 requests/min (peaks last ~10-20 minutes, a few times/day).
- Prompt/response lengths: median prompt ~120 tokens, 95th prompt ~420 tokens. Median response ~240 tokens; 95th response ~1,200 tokens for long-form summarization/rewrite jobs.
- Session/affinity: roughly 65% of traffic is session-based (same user, KV-cache hits plausible).
- Model mix: primary: open-chat-v2 (quantized 8-bit), reranker: rank-lite, heavy summarization uses finetuned-large.
- SLOs: p95 latency target 150-200ms for interactive flows; p99 is negotiable but important during bursts.

We want to understand whether a Redwood Dedicated footprint can absorb these bursts without degrading p95 beyond 200ms, and what a starting reserved commit would look like. Can we do a small replay with our traffic sample? Attached is a 6-hour traffic replay (sanitized) — lumos-sample-traffic-replay.jsonl.

Also curious about:
- autoscale reaction times vs. burst windows (10–20 minutes)
- recommendations for GPU mix (cost-sensitive) and acceptable batching heuristics for this workload

Thanks — Kai

--
Kai Watanabe
Head of Platform
Lumos AI
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity feasibility — Peak bursts & tail latency

Hi Kai — thanks for the detailed note and the replay file, that helps a lot. We can definitely run a replay in a controlled dedicated sandbox and produce a short report showing:
- effective throughput and observed p50/p95/p99 under different GPU mixes
- batching efficiency and token-economics per model variant
- cache-hit sensitivity (we'll toggle simulated KV cache hit rates)

Quick clarifying questions before we schedule the replay:
1) When you say 65% session affinity, is that per-user sticky routing (same KV across requests) or just repeat prompt similarity?
2) For the finetuned-large model, do you currently serve that in 16-bit or a quantized format?
3) Do you have a hard upper-bound on monthly committed spend or preferred GPU SKUs?

We've attached a short template (burst-mapping-template.xlsx) if you want to drop in observed percentiles and a brief token histogram — that speeds our preflight.

If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute technical call tomorrow to walk through the inputs. Happy to loop Karthik and Tessa to map to a Dedicated commit & canary plan.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kai Watanabe <kai@lumosai.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity feasibility — Peak bursts & tail latency

Hi Kai — looping in commercial context. A few quick notes on the commercial path while Naomi runs the replay:
- We can present two provisional reserved options after the replay: a lean starter commit (sized for steady-state + 2x typical burst allowance) and a resilience commit (steady-state + 4x burst cushion).
- Starter commits often use a mixed-GPU pool (one or two H100s or equivalent + a set of A100 40GBs for quantized inferencing) to balance cost and p99 headroom.
- We can also propose a short-term burst buffer (pre-bought burst credits) for the first 90 days while we observe real traffic.

I'll prepare a pro forma for both options once we have the replay results. Can we tentatively plan a commercial review next week?

Thanks,
Marissa
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, Kai Watanabe <kai@lumosai.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity feasibility — Peak bursts & tail latency

Thanks for the context, Kai. A few technical heuristics up front based on the profile you provided:
- Assumptions: median prompt 120 tokens + median response 240 => median total 360 tokens. Peak jobs (1,620 tokens) are the outliers driving p99 cost.
- Cache assumptions: with 65% session affinity and an expected 45-55% effective KV hit rate we can often reduce average tokens processed per request by ~30%. We'll test hit rates 0%, 30%, 50% in the replay.
- Initial GPU mix recommendation (provisional):
  • 3 x H100 80GB (for finetuned-large and p99 headroom)
  • 6 x A100 40GB (for quantized primary models; better cost per token with batching)
  • Optional: 2 x L4 or RTX-class nodes for light-weight reranker/embeddings to reduce spend on high-end SKUs.
- Batching & latency tradeoff: set dynamic batching with a 12–18ms batch window for interactive flows and an aggressive 40–50ms window for summarization endpoints. We will measure effective p95 impact in the replay — often small with lower queuing at these batch-window ranges.
- Autoscale behavior: dedicated autoscaling is typically configured to pre-warm capacity on sustained 60–90s elevated signals; however, short marketing-driven spikes (10–20m) are often best handled by a small standing buffer + burst credits.

Next steps from our side:
1) Run the sanitized 6-hour replay in the Redwood dedicated sandbox (we'll cap network/IO differences).
2) Produce a 2-pager with observed latencies and recommended commit (starter vs resilience) including a cost delta.
3) If results look good, propose a 2-week canary rollout plan to validate in production with a guarded traffic ramp.

Can you drop a small token distribution CSV for the models (if available) — that helps with kernel selection & batching knobs. Thanks!

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
